text:
sarah_sales: Quick presales POC update \/ question. Customer insists that both inference traffic and encryption keys remain within AWS Wavelength (us-east-1-wl1). They want BYO-KMS inside their VPC and an attestation that any sub-processors on the data path are carrier-only. Any immediate red flags?
ops_oncall: Short version: hosted control plane in wl zones = no. For Dedicated or Private we can run inference compute in wl1 if the customer provides carrier peering (ENI / MACVLAN), but note: 1) control-plane signaling (auth, rollouts) currently terminates in our control plane region and would still reach us-east-1, 2) some of our agents emit minimal telemetry to ops region unless we explicitly disable those hooks for the POC.
eng_infra: Technical addenda: we can validate runtime on the specific instance SKU, but need infra ticket for driver/kernel checks. Also confirm that the customer's WL1 subnet exposes the right DHCP routes and that MTU matches our container networking. Regarding sub-processors: carriers like "MegaTel Wireless" are separate legal entities; we can produce an attestation of network-only subproc involvement but cannot unilaterally rewrite their contracts.
privacy_legal: If the customer requires carrier-only subprocessor commitment we need a scoped legal exception and DPA appendix. Ask them to share the exact legal entity name for MegaTel (regional entity vs parent). Also need to know if audit logs must stay in-zone or can be stored in customer-managed S3 in us-east-1.
sarah_sales: Got it. They listed carrier as "MegaTel Wireless, Inc (US-East)" in the RFP. They also asked for an ops-usable snippet demonstrating routing preference + deterministic fallback sequencing for the POC. Can you provide a sample config we can send?
sre_pete: Sharing a minimal routing policy example. Emphasize that fallback will land to standard us-east-1 compute and that we will run a canary routing test during POC. Also note: prefix/KV caching is disabled by default in WL zones to avoid cross-zone egress unless customer approves a shared cache disk.

```json
{
  "routing_policy": "string:policy",
  "preferred_zone": "us-east-1-wl1",
  "fallback_order": ["us-east-1", "us-east-2"],
  "require_byo_kms": "true",
  "kms_endpoint": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/EXAMPLE",
  "telemetry_mode": "minimal",
  "kv_caching": "disabled",
  "canary": "enabled"
}
```

eng_infra: Ops notes to include with the snippet: 1) Customer must supply ENI / carrier peering docs and the BYO-KMS endpoint reachable from their WL1 VPC, 2) Provide expected QPS and max sequence length so we can size the wl pool (POC QPS ~5 is fine), 3) Confirm if token-level logs or traces are allowed to egress; if not, we'll disable them for the POC.
deploy-bot: Provision ticket created: PR-9182 (wl1 validation), ETA 72h.
ops_oncall: Operational blockers checklist for the customer: - Carrier POA and peering contact - BYO-KMS ARN + endpoint + IAM principal for Redwood runtime - Network diagrams showing ENI and route tables - Expected traffic profile (RPS, concurrency, seq len) - SLA for staying in WL vs allowed fallback
sarah_sales: I'll collect the docs and the KMS ARN. Customer said they can provide MegaTel POA and ENI details today. I'll update once I have artifacts. Thanks all :pray:
